## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people divided by the combined number of employed and unemployed people. It does not include everyone who is not working: people outside the labor force are counted separately.

A person who was not employed during the reference week may qualify as unemployed without actively searching if they are on temporary layoff and expect to be recalled. They must also be available for work, except for temporary illness.

Browsing job listings alone is different. It counts as passive-only search; active job-search efforts generally need to take place during the four-week period ending with the reference week.

So neither not working nor looking at listings alone determines whether someone is counted as unemployed. Classification depends on availability, the timing of the survey, and whether the person meets the active-search or temporary-layoff-and-recall condition.
